description: A normative framework, tactical catalog, and empirical baseline for authorship strategy under AI-mediated diffusion. The framework rests on a three-axis inversion (scarcity to diffusion, exclusivity to derivation, enclosure to openness) and a four-layer judgment stack (authenticity, attribution diffusion, idea-versus-scaffold separation, tactics). The tactical catalog formalizes twenty-one decisions extracted from operating a DOI-registered research ecosystem of four sibling repositories: concept DOI as canonical reference, DOI federation via .zenodo.json, cross-platform dataset federation (GitHub, Zenodo, Hugging Face Datasets), authorship metadata with ORCID auto-update disabled, audience-driven README localization, LLM-first ingest via dual entry points, human-attention platform signals excluded as a success metric, RAG-era attribution diffusion as two channels (parametric and retrieval), dual entry points rebalanced to asymmetric roles, vocabulary discipline (coin terms sparingly, anchor them densely to existing vocabulary and prior literature), a two-channel probe protocol measuring each diffusion channel by its own instrument, link-index-only contributions to external collections under a four-condition host audit, intrinsic content-derived identifiers (SWHID) as a priority-claim layer complementing the extrinsic DOI, implementation tracking as a two-tier ledger (a private operational ledger and its dated, effect-claim-free public projection) with periodic gap-review, license selection by an artifact's dominant audience rather than its surface form, and genre-split placement (essays as a repository-corpus canonical on an intrinsic identifier, papers as a concept-DOI canonical, with syndicated copies bound by entity federation), failure-mode diagnostics (a detector and a recovery strategy for each of the three acknowledged failure modes, with a diagnostic held as a failure-detector rather than a success metric), origin-claim falsifiability (testing a priority claim against prior art before publishing it and rescoping it to its narrowest defensible form), the structural-optimization-versus-content-authenticity boundary (optimizing the transmission path is legitimate, deforming the content to win citations is not), and onboarding to third-party AI-derived repository surfaces (a paraphrasing synthetic wiki used as a regurgitation-test drift diagnostic, a verbatim documentation hub whose access-count badge is a measurement signal not a metric, derived views blessed rather than gated). An empirical section reports preliminary observations from twenty-four days of CC0-published traffic data across the four sibling repositories, plus a probe baseline from the first run of the two-channel probe protocol, with explicit limitations on sample size and the absence of pre-versus-post intervention comparison. Sibling research lines (Agent Knowledge Cycle, Contemplative Agent, Agent Attribution Practice, Attention Not Self) are referenced but not extended. Written from a maker's and practitioner's stance: the academic apparatus used throughout (DOI, SWHID, citation graphs) is tooling for citability, durability, and traceability rather than an identity or destination, and the intended audience spans developers, practitioners, learners, and creative reusers across languages, with academic citation as one channel among several.
name: Authorship Strategy: A Normative Framework and Tactical Catalog for AI-Era Authenticity Inversion, with Empirical Grounding from a Four-Repository Research Ecosystem
